clue.text: He's left the money demanded in this bar

indicators.note: read as 'he is left' meaning the pair of letters he has departed from the next word, the

parts.note: a ransom is the money demanded by kidnappers

explanation.surface: Someone has walked out of a pub, leaving the ransom cash behind on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's left' tells you HE goes from 'the', leaving T. The bar is the crosspiece over a door or window, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbeam, especially one above a door or window.

clue.text: Intelligence shown in a little final piece from US

indicators.note: shown in means the information appears inside the next piece

parts.note: a tad, mainly American usage, is a small amount
gen is British slang for information or intelligence

explanation.surface: A spy shares a little last scrap of information from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From US' points to TAD, an American word for a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag end is the last remnant or tail of something.

clue.text: Woodcutter who had a couple of scores to settle

definitions.text: Woodcutter who had a couple of scores to settle

parts.words: Woodcutter who had a couple of scores to settle
parts.note: a couple of scores is forty, recalling the poor woodcutter of the Arabian Nights who outwitted forty thieves

explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero is a woodcutter who defeats the band of forty thieves.

clue.text: Those who know the ropes may be prophets keeping at a distance

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: seers are prophets who see the future
afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: Prophets keep their distance from experienced old hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know the ropes' is literal: sailors handle ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors know ropes literally, handling rigging at sea.

clue.text: Completes the sentence and establishes a proposition?

definitions.meaning: ends a sentence by putting down a full stop

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, placing a full stop; idiomatically, conveying an argument persuasively.

clue.text: Soft, like some land in story about sower?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
arable describes land fit for ploughing and crops

explanation.surface: A farming tale contrasting soft soil with ploughland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sower is one of the Gospel parables, the story of seed falling on different ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus's tale of the sower is a well-known instructive story told in the Gospels.

clue.text: Such a number should be kept secret and secure

definitions.text: Such a number should be kept secret
definitions.meaning: a personal identification number for a bank card must stay private
to secure something by fastening it with a peg

explanation.definitionFit: A bank card's personal code is private; as a verb, the word means fasten.

clue.text: One with zero urge to reform?

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rascal who has no desire whatever to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole description of the rascal, though only 'One' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest person, a single individual described as a rascal.

clue.text: Support against trouble may be just bluster

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
v (versus) means against
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Backing given against trouble may only be empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful show of boldness, a blustering display.

clue.text: Facilitate middle of text on page getting revised, cut

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters of the word text
cut means the end of the word is clipped off

parts.note: edited means revised

explanation.surface: An editor cuts and revises text on a page to smooth things along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' gives EX from TEXT; 'cut' clips the final D from EDITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to speed up a process or make it easier.

clue.text: What shows smile lapping milk, a funny old cat

indicators.note: lapping here means wrapping round, like a lap of cloth, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a grin is what shows a smile

indicators.note: funny means odd or strange, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grinning cat laps up its milk, looking comical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lapping' pretends the cat is drinking; it means wrapping round, and 'funny' makes IMALK from the milk and the a.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimalkin is an archaic word for a cat, especially an old she-cat.

clue.text: Get hold of doctor to contain most of inflammation

indicators.note: to contain asks the doctor's letters to hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a rash is a skin inflammation

explanation.surface: A patient seeks a doctor to deal with an inflamed patch.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize or take a firm hold of something.

clue.text: Antelope that's invaded many a laager?

indicators.note: the animal has invaded the words, so its letters sit inside the phrase many a laager

explanation.surface: An antelope has wandered into many a Boer wagon camp.
explanation.walkthrough: A laager is a defensive circle of wagons, as used by Boer settlers in southern Africa, where this antelope lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Handyman working round the flats

parts.note: reads like a caretaker in a block of flats, but flats are painted scenery boards in a theatre, so this is a theatre worker

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre crew member moves scenery flats and props about backstage.

clue.text: A note about girl leading guys in successful outcome

indicators.note: about means the note's letters go round the others

parts.note: a chit is a short note

indicators.note: leading puts the girl first, ahead of the guys

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
men are guys

explanation.surface: A message about a girl at the head of a group of lads ends happily.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is something successfully accomplished.

clue.text: Passed on and became genuinely autobiographical?

definitions.meaning: passed on is a euphemism for died
a memoir is genuine when the writer abandons the ghostwriter who would otherwise have produced it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for dying, read literally, means dropping one's hired writer and penning the memoir oneself.

clue.text: Favours theatrical acts worthy of applause

definitions.meaning: a turn is a performer's act; a good one deserves clapping

explanation.definitionFit: Helpful deeds are kindnesses; in variety theatre a turn is a single act on the bill.

clue.text: Jack, and what he did reportedly-. — descended at speed

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, as is AB, able seaman

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the sound of the words is used, not the spelling

parts.note: a sailor sailed

explanation.surface: A sailor recounts how he once came down quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack tar sails; AB plus a word sounding like SAILED gives ABSEILED, coming down a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face rapidly on a rope.

clue.text: Brisk new horse'd get broken in here?

indicators.note: get broken signals that the letters are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A lively young horse is due to be trained to the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: BERKSHIRE DOWNS is chalk upland in southern England, home to racehorse training around Lambourn, so horses really are broken in here.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorse trainers school and break young horses on these chalk hills west of London.

clue.text: University's interpretation

definitions.meaning: The name of an English university town, west of London
one way of understanding a text

explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a university in Berkshire; it is also a way of construing something.

clue.text: Plane finally unable to manoeuvre in clouds

indicators.note: to manoeuvre means moved about, so the letters are shifted into a new order
finally points to the last letter of the word plane

explanation.surface: A plane stuck in cloud cannot move about at last.
explanation.walkthrough: E from 'Plane finally' joins UNABLE, and 'to manoeuvre' rearranges all six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are interstellar clouds of gas and dust.

clue.text: Boy attending a pianist's performance

parts.note: a son is a boy
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: A lad goes along to a piano recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is an instrumental composition, often played by a pianist.

clue.text: English woman's ornament on uniform

parts.note: Paulette is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman wears a decoration on her uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is a decorative shoulder piece on a military uniform.

clue.text: Faithful, say, when taken in by deception

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside another word

parts.note: a lie is a deception
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A loyal follower is fooled by a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Liege as an adjective means loyal, bound by feudal allegiance.

clue.text: To show disapproval following thanks is socially unacceptable

indicators.note: following places the disapproving sound after the thanks

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Booing straight after being thanked is simply not done.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by social custom is off-limits and not to be mentioned or done.

clue.text: Tours developed on both sides of this river

definitions.text: Tours developed on both sides of this river

parts.words: Tours developed on both sides of this river
parts.note: Tours looks like trips, but it is the French city, which grew up straddling a major French waterway

explanation.definitionFit: France's longest river flows through the city of Tours in the Loire Valley.

clue.text: As rebel, fighter, argue terribly about right and wrong

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, with the rearranged letters going round the others
terribly means badly done, so the letters of argue are rearranged

parts.note: ill can mean wrong or harm, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: A rebel soldier argues furiously over questions of right and wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As rebel, fighter' reads as part of the story, yet it is the definition; 'terribly' makes GUERA, which 'about' wraps round the right-and-wrong pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular fighter in a small independent band, often a rebel against a government.

clue.text: Boasting when decline is reversed

indicators.note: is reversed means the word for decline is read from the end backwards

parts.note: to sag is to decline or droop

explanation.surface: Bragging happens when a slump is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is informal for empty boastful talk.

clue.text: Australians in mining group

definitions.meaning: slang for Australian (and New Zealand) soldiers or people
people who dig, such as miners in a goldfield

explanation.definitionFit: The slang for Aussie soldiers dates from goldfield miners, so both senses are excavators.

clue.text: Little girl needs a lot of time to make a bit of mosaic

parts.note: Tess is a short form of the girl's name Teresa
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A small girl takes ages to piece together a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small cubes of stone or glass laid to form a mosaic.
